gloss: abruptly; suddenly; out of the blue

definitions.gloss: abruptly; suddenly; out of the blue
definitions.explanation: Describes something happening without warning or preparation, often with an implication that the action is unexpected, rude, or jarring to others.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{唐突|とうとつ}に⟦{立|た}ち{上|あ}がった→立ち上がる：02128_tachiagaru⟧。
{唐突|とうとつ}な⟦{質問|しつもん}→質問：00888_shitsumon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません→申し訳ありません：21409_moushiwakearimasen⟧。
examples.english: I'm sorry for the sudden question.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{途中|とちゅう}→途中：01684_tochuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{唐突|とうとつ}に⟦{話題|わだい}→話題：03793_wadai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{変|か}えられて→変える：01089_kaeru⟧、⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦{戸惑|とまど}った→戸惑う：06036_tomadou⟧。
examples.english: Everyone was confused when the topic was abruptly changed in the middle of the meeting.

notes:
Conveys not just suddenness but often inappropriateness or social awkwardness — doing something without proper buildup or context. Frequently used when someone's behavior catches others off guard in a way that feels slightly rude or out of place.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {唐突|とうとつ}な⟦{質問|しつもん}→質問：00888_shitsumon⟧: an abrupt question
- {唐突|とうとつ}な⟦{訪問|ほうもん}→訪問：03622_houmon⟧: an unexpected visit
- {唐突|とうとつ}な⟦{発言|はつげん}→発言：05099_hatsugen⟧: an out-of-the-blue remark
- {唐突|とうとつ}に⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧: to ask out of nowhere

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{突然|とつぜん}→突然：00409_totsuzen⟧: suddenly — neutral; emphasizes unexpectedness without the nuance of social awkwardness
- ⟦{不意|ふい}→不意：11351_fui⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: unexpectedly — emphasizes being caught unprepared
- ⟦{急|きゅう}→急：13042_kyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: suddenly; quickly — the most common and casual option, also covers physical speed changes
